value.title: Implementation guide — Claude Code direct delivery (req-0002)

sections.name: architecture
sections.value: REQUIREMENT: .harness/government/prd/base-prd.dd.json req-0002 on the prime-governance branch, standing worktree /Users/jordanknight/pi-hacking/pij-worktrees/pij-governance/ — READ THE ROW VERBATIM; its note is the design input and it is longer than this section. EVIDENCE BASE, first-party and measured 2026-08-31 by pij-fatal-woodpecker (the PM for this plan): scratch/woodpecker-poc/FINDINGS.md plus frommode_poc.py (the BLIND v1) and frommode_poc2.py (the fixed instrument) — both kept so the instrument failure stays legible. THE SUBJECT is crates/transport/src/uds.rs in this repo, the shipped Rust UDS transport, plus the daemon delivery path that consumes it. FOUR DEFECTS TO FIX, all measured, none hypothesised: (B-2) from="uds:pij-daemon" is not a resolvable socket address, so the receiving CLI skips the hold receipt entirely and send_frame times out into Delivered{InjectedToTransport} — a message parked behind a human's approval dialog is reported delivered; (B-2b) classify_status requires type=="peer_message_status" while the real wire is {"type":"control","action":"peer_message_status"} — the bare form documented in fork issue #311 never appeared across four arms — so Status::Held is unreachable for TWO INDEPENDENT reasons and fixing the address alone will not surface it; its test at uds.rs:729 constructs the status line directly, which is why the suite is green over an unreachable path; (B-3) status frames carry NO correlation id anywhere in the lifecycle (own fresh uuid, no orig_msg_id/dropped_msg_ids/wereHeld) and DENIALS are uncorrelatable to their own HOLDS — measured with 3 frames in flight: 2 held + 2 denied lines byte-identical but for uuids. Whether arrival order is send order is UNTESTABLE FROM THE WIRE, because verifying it needs the correlation the frames lack; (B-1) registration does not adopt the spawned identity, so a daemon-spawned seat strands a phantom pre-bind row on the same pane with the same spawn_id — and rpc_port is stamped on THAT row, so the live row a consumer reads carries no port. BINDING INVARIANT, ruled by o-prime and not open for re-litigation by this plan: correlation is POSITIONAL — ONE MESSAGE IN FLIGHT PER CONNECTION, concurrency REFUSED at the transport rather than resolved. The identical constraint was forced on Copilot RPC by plan 109's F0-3 via an entirely independent argument; two harnesses, two derivations, one transport-layer law. CONSENT: from-mode="bypass" is delivered to a --dangerously-skip-permissions recipient with no dialog; without it the message is HELD. Proven on both arms by three independent observers (sender status line, recipient transcript, operator's screen). CORRECTED AT THE PM ACK (my claim was false; woodpecker read the tree): crossSessionInbound=accept IS fully implemented — crates/harnesses/src/spawn.rs:6, :130-135, :163-165 (the capability is DERIVED from the emitted args, not asserted), tests at :300/:305 and crates/cli/tests/spawn.rs:207-208. The real gap: it is opt-in and DEFAULTS FALSE (`pij spawn --accept-inbound`, crates/cli/src/main.rs:134-136, passed by nobody), and uds.rs can_deliver/deliver refuse without it — SO THE UDS TRANSPORT IS OFF FOR EVERY SEAT ON THE FLEET TODAY, not broken, not reached. Whether it defaults ON for daemon-spawned Claude seats is a CONSENT POLICY question for the operator, not this plan. WHY send-keys dies: macOS pty hands 1022-byte chunks, so a body over that arrives as ONLY ITS TAIL (8/8 on 2.1.246) and the legacy submit oracle matches the surviving tail and reports confirmed over lost data. PRIOR ART: fork vaughanknight/pij v0.2.0, issue #311, handover docs/handover/v0.2.0/ — first-party for Claude and measured (177ms, 0 keystrokes, byte-exact at 3KB), but VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING: plan 109 tested its Copilot half against the installed CLI and 4 of 6 claims diverged. Their `acked` is written at injection and proves injected-to-socket, never read — our honest-receipt vocabulary (Delivered{origin}/Queued/Held{reason}/SeatIsGone) is ahead of theirs and MUST NOT regress to it.

value.rationale: Two units with a frozen seam between them and near-zero shared files: u-uds owns the transport (crates/transport/src/uds.rs + its tests), u-adopt owns registration identity adoption (the daemon register path + seat descriptor). They touch different crates and are ordered only by review, not by code. The PM (woodpecker) authored the evidence base, so it composes and may code u-uds itself if a coder would cost more context than it saves — that is the PM's call at dispatch, recorded in the packet. A third unit is deliberately NOT created for crossSessionInbound-at-spawn: it edits the spawn path u-adopt already owns.

value.name: honest UDS transport: routable reply address, real wire shape, positional correlation
value.paths: crates/transport/src/uds.rs and its tests; crates/daemon/src/delivery/** only where the transport contract forces it (name the lines in the receipt)
value.responsibility: Make Held/Denied OBSERVABLE and honest: bind a reply listener inside the recipient's socket namespace and advertise a routable from=; accept the real status shape (type==control, action==peer_message_status) and prove the bare form is not emitted; enforce one message in flight per connection and REFUSE concurrency rather than resolving it; carry from-mode=bypass; keep the honest-receipt vocabulary — a timeout is never Delivered.
value.interface: Transport trait unchanged; DeliveryOutcome vocabulary unchanged (Delivered{origin}/Queued/Held{reason}/SeatIsGone). Any change to either is a seam change and comes to the prime at the ack, not after.
value.test_strategy: Acceptance uses the RECIPIENT-SIDE DISCRIMINATOR, never presence/absence: held/denied leaves a type=system record, delivered leaves a queue-operation followed by a real type=user turn — a positive artifact on BOTH sides. Every guard must be witnessed RED before its green counts: mutate from= back to the unroutable form (hold receipt must vanish), mutate the status matcher back to the bare type (Held must become unreachable), put two messages in flight (the transport must refuse, not guess). A test that constructs a status line directly proves nothing about the wire — uds.rs:729 is the anti-pattern, do not repeat it.
value.note: woodpecker's frommode_poc2.py is the reference instrument — port its discovery and its timing discipline, do not re-derive. Discovery: ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json carries messagingSocketPath AND a tmux field; resolve by descriptor pid, else scan records for tmux ending .<paneId>; TWO claude homes exist (~/.claude and ~/.claude-alt). Timestamp every inbound line as a monotonic delta from send so a machine outcome is separable from one gated on a human click, and record any operator click as an INPUT.

value.name: registration adopts the spawned identity; crossSessionInbound at spawn
value.paths: the daemon register route + seat descriptor/registry in crates/daemon and crates/store; the spawn path where Claude seats are launched
value.responsibility: A daemon-spawned seat that registers must ADOPT its pre-bind row rather than minting a second one — one seat, one row, the stamped rpc_port surviving onto the row consumers read. And spawn Claude seats with `--settings '{"crossSessionInbound":"accept"}'` so consent is configured honestly rather than self-asserted per message.
value.interface: Seat descriptor shape and the register request/response; changing either is a seam change for the prime.
value.test_strategy: Witness must be built FROM THE LAUNCHED ENVIRONMENT, never from the spawn response — that substitution hid plan 109's F9 for three heads. Discriminating arm: register a seat WITHOUT a fresh allocation immediately preceding it (re-register an existing seat), which is the case the old acceptance test could not produce. Prove one row, not two, on the same pane with the same spawn_id.
value.note: This is B-1, ruled blocking for the Copilot RPC unit too — fixing it here unblocks that as a side effect. Live evidence of the defect: allocated pij-irregular-apocalypse vs a second row pij-empirical-caribou, same pane %1963, same spawn_id. ROOT CAUSE FOUND AT THE ACK (woodpecker): crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:366-370 adopts the pre-bind row BY SEAT ID ALONE, but the pre-bind row was created under an allocated memorable id (:443/:649) while the registering process claims a different one — the find misses, a fresh descriptor is minted, the allocated row strands. Worse, :371-376 computes binds_spawned_incarnation from a spawn_id match only AFTER that id-keyed find has failed, so at :400 the fresh rpc_port_intent is CLEARED on the very registration it was stamped for. FIX DIRECTION RULED: adopt on spawn_id (+pane) when the id lookup misses — one lookup change plus the port-preservation consequence, no new abstraction, seam untouched.

Coders get their own worktrees off s110/claude-delivery; the PM merges, coders never merge — two coders on one branch is forbidden (a routine `git checkout -- .` by one reverts the other's landed commit and stages it as ordinary authorship). ABSOLUTE PATHS in every packet. Per-worktree CARGO_TARGET_DIR, never a shared one — a shared target served artefacts compiled from another seat's unpushed source and produced a false red. AND: whoever creates a worktree owns reaping it; an isolation mechanism ships with its reaper.

value.steps: Ask each done coder its ASSUMPTIONS before merging. Merge u-adopt first (identity is upstream of anything that reads a row), then u-uds. Re-run the full gate on the COMPOSED, REBASED tree — a green on a unit branch is not a green on the composition. Declare one head and prove the fix and the head agree; a receipt measured at a head nobody merged is the defect this fleet keeps re-finding.
value.integration_proof: AMENDED AT THE ACK (woodpecker objection 2, upheld): the two arms are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE ON ONE SEAT, because crossSessionInbound=accept is exactly the setting that stops the recipient holding. The rig must therefore name two recipient configurations explicitly: HELD ARM against a recipient WITHOUT the accept setting (a hand-started seat, as in the PoC) — held observed from the sender side BEFORE any human click, any operator click recorded as an INPUT; DELIVERED ARM against a seat spawned WITH --accept-inbound — bypass-marked message delivered with no dialog and byte-exact above 1022 bytes. Both arms, three observers (sender status line, recipient transcript, operator's screen). A single-seat rig cannot produce both and will either fake the held arm or re-open r1 by concluding Held is unreachable for a third reason.

value.when: after composition, before the PR into main
value.inputs: req-0002 verbatim + this impl-guide + full branch diff + woodpecker's FINDINGS.md; priority order: (1) is Held actually observable on the wire, or still unreachable for a third reason nobody has named; (2) is concurrency REFUSED rather than resolved; (3) is every guard witnessed red before its green; (4) does the honest-receipt vocabulary still refuse to call a timeout Delivered; (5) one row per seat, proven from the launched environment.
value.model_override: cross-model from the o-prime's team settings; the reviewer must re-derive the acceptance arms by execution, not read them

value.text: A third independent reason Held stays unreachable, discovered after the first two are fixed — retired by making the FIRST commit a failing observation test that proves Held reachable end to end on the live CLI, before any refactor.

Building on the fork's spec where it does not match the installed build — retired by verifying each borrowed claim against Claude CLI 2.1.251 before it becomes code; 4 of 6 of that spec's Copilot claims diverged when tested.

Silently resolving concurrency instead of refusing it (a positional transport minting a false Delivered for a message no human released) — retired by the two-in-flight mutation: the transport must refuse, and the test must fail if it guesses.

An acceptance test written against the spawn response rather than the launched environment — retired by the u-adopt discriminating arm (re-register with no fresh allocation) and by the review priority list.

Regressing the honest-receipt vocabulary toward the fork's `acked` (injected-to-socket reported as read) — retired by keeping Delivered{origin} and by a test that a 15s silence is never upgraded past InjectedToTransport.
